sources.title: Genie: Generative Interactive Environments
sources.notes: The paper reports the final dynamics-model recipe and scaling studies.

sources.title: GAIA-1: A Generative World Model for Autonomous Driving
sources.notes: The paper reports data splits and separate autoencoder, world-model, and decoder recipes.

sources.title: Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI
sources.notes: The paper reports data curation scale and progressive training, but not one universal recipe.

sources.title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
sources.notes: DreamerV3 is an online RL/world-model system; its domain-independent claims are not a video pretraining recipe.

sources.title: Diffusion Forcing: Next-token Prediction Meets Full-Sequence Diffusion
sources.notes: The paper explicitly limits its experiments and does not claim internet-scale training.

sources.title: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning
sources.notes: The paper separates internet-scale representation pretraining from a small action-conditioned robot post-training stage.

recipes.objective: Autoregressive latent-video dynamics with learned latent actions.

dataset.name: Platformers
dataset.scale_description: 6.8M clips, each 16 seconds at 10 FPS; the paper also reports 55M filtered candidates.

sequence.horizon_description: 16-second clips; autoregressive rollout beyond the training clip is evaluated.

compute.notes: Final dynamics model; tokenizer and latent action model are separate components.

recipes.checkpoint_policy: Paper reports final training budget and scaling curves; checkpoint selection details are not specified.

evidence.claim: 10.1B dynamics model, batch 512, 125k steps on 256 TPUv5p
Dynamics-model max learning rate 3e-5 and 5k warmup

limitations: This is a large-scale platformer foundation model, not a transferable default for Ctrl-World.
Reported values are a literature prior and have no local VerdiWM validation receipt.

recipes.objective: Action-, text-, and unconditional-conditioned driving video world model.

dataset.name: Proprietary London driving data
dataset.scale_description: 4,700 hours at 25 Hz (about 420M unique images); 400 hours of disjoint validation runs.

sequence.horizon_description: Decoder sequences use seven images; source data supports 6.25, 12.5, and 25 Hz tasks.

optimization.scheduler: linear warmup then cosine decay to 1e-5

compute.notes: World-model training uses DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 and activation checkpointing.

recipes.checkpoint_policy: Independent validation runs/geofences are described; best-checkpoint selection is not specified.

evidence.claim: 4,700 hours and about 420M unique images, with 400 hours of validation data
100k steps, batch 128 split across 64 A100 80GB GPUs
1e-4 AdamW learning rate, 2.5k warmup, cosine decay

limitations: The data is proprietary driving footage and not comparable to small robot-trajectory datasets.
The paper has separate component recipes; this entry covers the world-model component only.

recipes.objective: Diffusion and autoregressive world-foundation-model pretraining followed by specialization.

dataset.name: Cosmos curated video corpus
dataset.scale_description: About 20M raw video hours; about 100M pretraining clips and 10M fine-tuning clips after curation.

sequence.horizon_description: Progressive training starts at 512px/57 frames and moves to 720px/121 frames.

optimization.scheduler: per-model schedule; high-quality fine-tuning uses linear decay for O(10k) iterations

compute.notes: The paper reports a cluster of 10,000 H100 GPUs over three months for reported WFM models.

recipes.checkpoint_policy: Progressive resolution/length stages and high-quality-subset fine-tuning; no universal best-checkpoint rule.

evidence.claim: 20M raw hours, 100M pretraining clips, 10M fine-tuning clips
High-quality fine-tuning uses O(10k) iterations with linear decay; universal batch and total pretraining steps are not given

limitations: Cosmos is a platform with multiple model families and stages; collapsing it to one recipe would be misleading.
The reported hardware scale is not a recommendation for a small local experiment.

recipes.objective: Learn latent dynamics from online interaction and improve policy through imagined rollouts.

dataset.name: Online environment interaction across 150+ tasks
dataset.scale_description: The paper evaluates more than 150 tasks; it is not a fixed offline video corpus.

sequence.horizon_description: Imagined rollout horizon is task/configuration dependent.

compute.notes: This entry deliberately records no guessed fixed training budget.

recipes.checkpoint_policy: Task evaluation is reported; a general best-checkpoint selection recipe is not disclosed.

evidence.claim: The system is evaluated across more than 150 diverse tasks
The paper is an online RL algorithm paper, not a fixed video-pretraining recipe

limitations: Do not use DreamerV3 figures as a batch/step prescription for action-conditioned video training.

recipes.objective: Train per-token diffusion noise levels to reduce autoregressive exposure bias and stabilize long rollouts.

dataset.name: Minecraft and DMLab gameplay videos
dataset.scale_description: The paper reports task datasets but explicitly does not study internet-scale pretraining.

sequence.horizon_description: Training windows and frame stacking vary by task; rollout is evaluated to 1000 frames.

compute.hardware: not disclosed as a scaling recipe
compute.notes: RNN implementation is chosen for efficient decision-making experiments.

recipes.checkpoint_policy: The paper reports validation/benchmark metrics; no universal checkpoint ladder is specified.

evidence.claim: Diffusion Forcing can roll out beyond the training horizon, including 1000 frames
The paper explicitly says it does not investigate internet-scale datasets and tasks

limitations: This is a mechanism/ablation reference, not a production pretraining recipe.

recipes.objective: Self-supervised mask denoising in representation space with EMA targets.

dataset.name: VideoMix22M and image/video sources
dataset.scale_description: Over 1M hours of internet video; data scaling from 2M to 22M videos.

sequence.horizon_description: Progressive training uses 16-frame clips in warmup/main phases and 64-frame clips in cooldown.

compute.notes: The paper reports compute in GPU-years for scaling studies rather than a single device count.

recipes.checkpoint_policy: Frozen representation probes and scaling ablations are used; no universal best-checkpoint rule.

evidence.claim: Over 1M hours of video and 22M videos after scaling
12k warmup, 228k constant phase, 12k cooldown; total 252k iterations
16-frame 256px warmup/main and longer/higher-resolution clips in cooldown

limitations: This is observation representation pretraining; it is not itself action-conditioned control training.

recipes.objective: Autoregressive future-feature prediction conditioned on actions and end-effector state over a frozen V-JEPA 2 representation.

dataset.name: DROID raw robot videos
dataset.scale_description: Less than 62 hours after discarding videos shorter than 4 seconds; left-camera views only.

sequence.horizon_description: Random 4-second clips at 4 FPS; 16 frames per training sample.

compute.notes: The encoder is frozen; the recipe is a small post-training stage, not foundation pretraining.

recipes.checkpoint_policy: The paper evaluates closed-loop planning and does not specify a general checkpoint-selection rule.

evidence.claim: Approximately 62 hours of unlabeled DROID robot video, usually 3-4 seconds per video
Batch 256; LR warms from 7.5e-5 to 4.25e-4 for 4.5k, holds 85.5k, then decays 4.5k

limitations: This is the closest public analogue to adapting a pretrained world representation on a small robot dataset, but it is not evidence that the same numbers fit Ctrl-World.
The encoder is frozen and the data split/camera convention is task-specific.
